did.unittitle: Kingston Lounge nightclub photographs and ephemera
did.abstract: Printed ephemera and photographs from the Kingston Lounge at 120 Kingston Avenue in Crown Heights from the late 1940s.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged into three folders by type: ephemera, staff photographs, and celebrity photographs.

bioghist.head: Historical note
bioghist.p: The Kingston Lounge opened on the southwest corner of Kingston Avenue and Bergen Street in Crown Heights in 1944. According to local history blogger Richard Nickel Jr., "during its heyday, the Kingston attracted guests from as far away as Harlem; even holding no more than 60 patrons at a time, the Lounge attracted musicians as renowned as Kenny Dorham, Randy Weston, Max Roach, Sahib Shihab and Matthew Gee. In fact, Dorham, Gee, Cecil Payne and company recorded a 1960 album under the name of The Swingers (Jazzland Records) on which the second track is entitled 'Kingston Lounge', in honor of the place where they practiced and jammed out, entertaining the block until the wee hours." The club did not admit white patrons until the 1970s. It fell into decline in the 1980s, and the building was abandoned by 2001.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: 31 items from the Kingston Lounge at 120 Kingston Avenue in Crown Heights, collected by former night bartender Wilfred Tibbs. Printed ephemera includes a souvenir menu from the club's 3rd anniversary celebration on 18 February 1947, a promotional handbill, and a business card of Wilfred Tibbs. The collection also includes publicity shots of Black entertainers, inscribed to Wilfred Tibbs, and candid photographs of the bar staff. The Kingston Lounge closed in 2001, and its neon signs were only removed very recently.

Celebrity subjects in the collection include The Charioteers, Dinah Washington, Gwen Tynes, Ida James, Cedric Wallace, Una Mae Carlisle, H. Byrd Moore, Melrose Colbert, Hadda Brooks, Dotty Saulters, The Gene Redd Trio, Lee Richardson, Eddie Vinson, Gene Strider, Maxine Sullivan, Teddy Brannon Trio, Rubel Blakely, Eddie Williams Trio, and Joe King.
